title: Leviticus Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Leviticus chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Leviticus Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Leviticus Chapter 11.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11:3, what characteristics must a beast have to be eaten?
options: Parteth the hoof, is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud
Cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof
Is a flying creeping thing with four legs
questions.correctAnswer: Parteth the hoof, is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:3 states that beasts which part the hoof, are clovenfooted, and chew the cud shall be eaten.

questions.question: Which animal is declared unclean because it chews the cud but does not divide the hoof?
questions.correctAnswer: Camel
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:4 declares the camel unclean because it cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof.

questions.question: True or False: The hare is considered clean because it chews the cud and has a divided hoof.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:6 states the hare cheweth the cud but divideth not the hoof and is unclean.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11:7 say about the swine?
options: It divideth the hoof, is clovenfooted, but does not chew the cud and is unclean
It is clean because it has fins and scales
It cheweth the cud and is clean
It is a flying creeping thing
questions.correctAnswer: It divideth the hoof, is clovenfooted, but does not chew the cud and is unclean
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:7 says the swine divideth the hoof and is clovenfooted but does not chew the cud; it is unclean.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 11:9, you may eat fish that have fins and scales.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:9 commands to eat all that have fins and scales in the waters.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT allowed to be eaten according to Leviticus 11:10?
options: All that have not fins and scales in the waters
Beasts that chew the cud and part the hoof
questions.correctAnswer: All that have not fins and scales in the waters
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:10 declares all in the waters without fins and scales an abomination and not to be eaten.

questions.question: Which bird is listed in Leviticus 11:13 as an abomination and not to be eaten?
questions.correctAnswer: Eagle
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:13 includes the eagle among the fowls that are abominations and shall not be eaten.

questions.question: True or False: The owl is among the birds that are an abomination and cannot be eaten.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:16 lists the owl as one of the birds that are an abomination and shall not be eaten.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11:15, which bird is considered an abomination after his kind?
questions.correctAnswer: Raven
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:15 states that every raven after his kind is an abomination.

questions.question: What are the characteristics of flying creeping things allowed to be eaten according to Leviticus 11:21-22?
options: They have legs above their feet to leap upon the earth
They divide the hoof and chew the cud
questions.correctAnswer: They have legs above their feet to leap upon the earth
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:21-22 states that flying creeping things with legs above their feet to leap are permitted to be eaten.

questions.question: True or False: According to Leviticus 11:8, it is clean to touch the carcase of swine.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:8 instructs not to eat their flesh or touch their carcase because they are unclean.

questions.question: Which of the following comes first in Leviticus 11:3-7 regarding animals?
options: Animals that part the hoof, are clovenfooted, and chew the cud are to be eaten
Animals that chew the cud but do not divide the hoof are unclean
Animals that divide the hoof but do not chew the cud are unclean
All flying creeping things with four legs are an abomination
questions.correctAnswer: Animals that part the hoof, are clovenfooted, and chew the cud are to be eaten
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:3 states the rule about beasts to eat before listing unclean animals in verses 4-7.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11:2, who is instructed to be spoken to about the beasts that may be eaten?
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:2 directs Moses and Aaron to speak to the children of Israel about the beasts they may eat.

questions.question: Which of these animals chews the cud but is unclean because it does not divide the hoof?
questions.correctAnswer: Coney
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:5 says the coney chews the cud but divideth not the hoof and is unclean.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11:12 say about creatures in the waters without fins and scales?
options: They are an abomination and shall not be eaten
They are clean and may be eaten
They are acceptable only if cooked
They are only unclean if dead
questions.correctAnswer: They are an abomination and shall not be eaten
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:12 declares that whatsoever hath no fins nor scales in the waters shall be an abomination.

medium.title: Leviticus Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Leviticus Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Which birds are specifically listed as abominations that shall not be eaten according to Leviticus 11?
questions.correctAnswer: Eagle, vulture, and raven
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:13-15 lists the eagle, ossifrage, ospray, vulture, kite, and every raven as abominable birds that shall not be eaten.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11, which of the following creeping flying things may be eaten?
options: All flying creeping things with four feet
All creeping things that creep upon the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Locust, bald locust, beetle, grasshopper
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:21-22 permits eating certain flying creeping things that have legs above their feet to leap upon the earth, such as the locust, bald locust, beetle, and grasshopper.

questions.question: What happens to a person who touches the carcass of any unclean flying creeping thing?
options: They shall be unclean until the evening
They must leave the camp for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be unclean until the evening
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:24 states that anyone who touches the carcass of unclean flying creeping things shall be unclean until the evening, showing the temporary nature of uncleanness.

questions.question: Which animals that go upon their paws are considered unclean according to Leviticus 11?
options: Beasts that go on all fours with paws
All cloven-footed beasts that chew the cud
Every beast that swims in rivers
questions.correctAnswer: Beasts that go on all fours with paws
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:27 specifies that beasts which go upon their paws among animals that go on all fours are unclean and touching their carcass causes uncleanness until evening.

questions.question: Which of the following creeping things are declared unclean and cause uncleanness when touched dead?
questions.correctAnswer: Weasel, mouse, tortoise, ferret
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:29-31 lists creeping things such as the weasel, mouse, tortoise, ferret, chameleon, lizard, snail, and mole as unclean and touching them dead causes uncleanness until evening.

questions.question: What must be done to any vessel or clothing that has a dead unclean creature fall upon it?
options: It must be put into water and it shall be unclean until the evening
It must be anointed with oil
It must be kept separate for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: It must be put into water and it shall be unclean until the evening
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:32 instructs that any vessel or clothing upon which a dead unclean creature falls must be put into water and remain unclean until evening to be cleansed.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11, what should be done with an earthen vessel into which an unclean creature falls?
options: It shall be purified with water
It shall be given to a priest
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be broken
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:33 states that any earthen vessel containing an unclean creature shall be broken, indicating the impurity cannot be cleansed by water alone.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11:34 say about meat on which water has been poured in a vessel that had contact with an unclean creature?
options: The meat shall be eaten with thanksgiving
The meat shall be offered as a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: The meat shall be unclean
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:34 explains that any meat on which such water has come shall be unclean, emphasizing the importance of avoiding contamination from unclean sources.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 11:35 instruct to treat ovens or ranges where parts of carcasses of unclean creatures have fallen?
options: They shall be washed with water
They shall be covered with earth
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be broken down
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:35 commands that ovens or ranges where unclean carcass parts fall shall be broken down due to their uncleanness, showing a strict measure to prevent defilement.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11:36 teach about fountains or pits with plenty of water that have contact with carcasses of unclean creatures?
options: The water remains clean, but what touches the carcass is unclean
The water becomes unclean and must be discarded
The water must be anointed with oil
questions.correctAnswer: The water remains clean, but what touches the carcass is unclean
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:36 clarifies that a fountain or pit with plenty of water remains clean even if an unclean carcass touches it, but the carcass itself becomes unclean, showing a distinction in contamination.

questions.question: If a beast that is permitted to be eaten dies, what is the consequence for a person who touches its carcass according to Leviticus 11?
options: They shall be unclean until the evening
They must offer a burnt offering
They must leave the camp for seven days
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be unclean until the evening
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:39 states that anyone touching the carcass of a beast that may be eaten if it dies shall be unclean until the evening, indicating temporary uncleanness.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11, what is the status of every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:41 declares that every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth is an abomination and shall not be eaten.

questions.question: Is the bat considered a clean bird that may be eaten according to Leviticus 11?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:19 includes the bat among the birds listed as abominations that shall not be eaten.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11:43 teach about making oneself unclean with creeping things?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:43 warns not to make yourselves abominable or unclean with any creeping thing that creeps, teaching obedience and holiness in everyday life.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Leviticus 11:44-45 for the Israelites to sanctify themselves and be holy?
options: Because God is holy and brought them out of Egypt
Because they must follow the priest's instructions
Because they want to be wealthy
Because they want to be powerful over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Because God is holy and brought them out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:44-45 states that the Israelites should be holy because the LORD their God is holy and because He brought them out of Egypt to be their God, emphasizing trust and obedience.

hard.title: Leviticus Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Leviticus Chapter 11.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11, what must be done with any earthen vessel into which an unclean thing falls?
questions.correctAnswer: It must be broken
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:33 states that every earthen vessel where any unclean thing falls shall be unclean and must be broken.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11 say about meat that has been touched by water that has been in an unclean vessel?
questions.correctAnswer: It is unclean
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:34 explains that all meat on which such water comes shall be unclean, as well as all drink in such vessels.

questions.question: What must be done to ovens or ranges on which any part of an unclean carcass falls?
options: They must be purified with fire
questions.correctAnswer: They must be broken down
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:35 commands that ovens or ranges where any part of an unclean carcass falls shall be broken down because they are unclean.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 11 differentiate between a fountain or pit and other water sources regarding cleanliness?
options: A fountain or pit with plenty of water is clean, but what touches an unclean carcass is unclean
A fountain or pit is always unclean
All water sources are clean regardless
questions.correctAnswer: A fountain or pit with plenty of water is clean, but what touches an unclean carcass is unclean
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:36 explains that a fountain or pit with plenty of water is clean, though anything touching an unclean carcass becomes unclean.

questions.question: If a carcass falls upon sowing seed before it is planted, what is its status according to Leviticus 11?
questions.correctAnswer: The seed remains clean
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:37 states that if any part of a carcass falls on seed to be sown, it shall be clean.

questions.question: When does sowing seed become unclean according to Leviticus 11?
options: If water is put upon the seed and any part of a carcass falls on it
If it is touched by an unclean person
If it is harvested with unclean tools
If it is planted on unclean ground
questions.correctAnswer: If water is put upon the seed and any part of a carcass falls on it
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:38 clarifies that if water is put on seed and any part of a carcass falls thereon, it becomes unclean.

questions.question: What is the status of a person who touches the carcass of a clean beast that has died?
options: They shall be unclean until the evening
They must wash with water only
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be unclean until the evening
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:39 states that anyone touching the carcass of a beast they may eat becomes unclean until evening.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11, what must one do after eating the carcass of a clean beast that died?
options: Wash clothes and be unclean until the evening
questions.correctAnswer: Wash clothes and be unclean until the evening
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:40 prescribes washing clothes and remaining unclean until evening after eating such carcasses.

questions.question: Which of the following is declared an abomination and not to be eaten according to Leviticus 11?
options: Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth
Beasts that chew the cud and have cloven hooves
Flying insects with legs above their feet to leap
questions.correctAnswer: Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:41 declares that every creeping thing upon the earth is an abomination and shall not be eaten.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11 say about creeping things that go upon the belly or have more feet?
options: They shall not be eaten and are an abomination
They are clean and may be eaten
Only those with more than four feet are unclean
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not be eaten and are an abomination
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:42 explains that things going upon the belly, all four, or having more feet among creeping things are abominations not to be eaten.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Leviticus 11:44-45 for Israel to sanctify themselves and be holy?
options: Because the LORD their God is holy and brought them out of Egypt
Because they are the chosen nation for sacrifices
Because they must avoid all contact with animals
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD their God is holy and brought them out of Egypt
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:44-45 states the LORD is holy and brought Israel out of Egypt; therefore, they must be holy and sanctify themselves.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of holiness and separation from unclean things as taught in Leviticus 11?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:15-16 echoes Leviticus 11’s call for holiness by quoting, 'Be ye holy; for I am holy,' paralleling the theme of separation from uncleanness.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word meaning 'unclean' or 'impure' is central to the dietary laws in Leviticus 11, reflecting ritual impurity?
questions.correctAnswer: Tamei
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Tamei' denotes ritual uncleanness or impurity, key in Leviticus 11’s dietary laws distinguishing clean and unclean.

questions.question: What literary device frames Leviticus 11 by beginning and ending with the purpose of distinguishing clean and unclean animals?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:1-2 and 11:46-47 form an inclusio, framing the chapter by stating its purpose to distinguish clean from unclean animals.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11:25, what must a person do if they carry any part of an unclean carcass?
options: Wash their clothes and be unclean until the evening
Remain clean if they do not touch their face
questions.correctAnswer: Wash their clothes and be unclean until the evening
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:25 commands that anyone carrying an unclean carcass must wash clothes and be unclean until evening.

theological.title: Leviticus Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Leviticus Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11:3, what are the two characteristics that define beasts which the Israelites are allowed to eat?
options: Parteth the hoof and is clovenfooted
Cheweth the cud and divideth the hoof
Parteth the hoof and is clovenfooted and cheweth the cud
Is clovenfooted and divideth the hoof
questions.correctAnswer: Parteth the hoof and is clovenfooted and cheweth the cud
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:3 explicitly states that beasts which part the hoof, are clovenfooted, and chew the cud are the ones the Israelites may eat. This reveals God's detailed criteria for clean animals.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the command in Leviticus 11:44 that the Israelites must be holy as God is holy?
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:44 calls for the Israelites to sanctify themselves and be holy, reflecting God's holiness. This is a clear call to sanctification, the process of being made holy.

questions.question: What divine attribute does Leviticus 11:45 emphasize when God says, 'For I am the LORD that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt'?
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:45 connects God’s act of deliverance with His holiness, commanding the people to be holy since He is holy. This demonstrates God's transcendent holiness.

questions.question: Which creatures are explicitly forbidden to be eaten because they lack fins and scales, according to Leviticus 11:10-12?
options: All creatures in the waters without fins and scales
Only creatures that move on land and water
questions.correctAnswer: All creatures in the waters without fins and scales
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:10-12 teaches that all water creatures lacking fins and scales are an abomination and must not be eaten, showing God's concern for purity and distinction in creation.

questions.question: How does the list of birds considered 'an abomination' in Leviticus 11:13-19 contribute to the theological theme of this chapter?
options: It underscores the theme of separation between clean and unclean animals
It shows God's preference for predatory birds
It emphasizes the importance of dietary diversity
It reflects cultural customs unrelated to holiness
questions.correctAnswer: It underscores the theme of separation between clean and unclean animals
questions.explanation: Verses 13-19 list birds considered unclean, reinforcing the chapter’s overarching theme of distinguishing between clean and unclean to maintain holiness.

questions.question: What is the significance of the rule in Leviticus 11:21-22 allowing the eating of certain flying creeping things with legs above their feet?
options: It shows God's allowance within His laws for specific exceptions
It indicates all insects are clean
It permits eating any animal with legs
It is a symbolic reference to angels
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's allowance within His laws for specific exceptions
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:21-22 permits eating specific flying creeping things with legs above their feet, demonstrating God's detailed and measured distinctions in clean and unclean animals.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do Leviticus 11:24-25 and Leviticus 11:39-40 provide about ritual purity?
options: Contact with unclean carcasses causes ritual impurity until evening
Eating clean animals results in impurity
Touching any animal carcass has no effect on purity
Purity laws only apply to priests
questions.correctAnswer: Contact with unclean carcasses causes ritual impurity until evening
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:24-25 and 39-40 explain that touching or bearing carcasses of unclean or even clean animals causes impurity until evening, showing the importance of ritual cleanliness.

questions.question: In what way does Leviticus 11:31-32 illustrate the concept of holiness in daily life?
options: It requires cleansing even from contact with dead unclean creatures
It permits casual contact with unclean animals
It only concerns temple rituals, not daily life
It allows eating unclean animals if washed
questions.correctAnswer: It requires cleansing even from contact with dead unclean creatures
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:31-32 mandates that touching dead unclean creatures causes impurity, requiring cleansing, which shows holiness extends into daily living practices.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that dietary laws in Leviticus 11 are outdated and irrelevant. What does Leviticus 11:44-45 actually teach about the purpose of these laws?
options: They are meant to sanctify the people because God is holy
They are merely cultural customs with no spiritual significance
They are symbolic of social hierarchy
They are intended only for health reasons
questions.correctAnswer: They are meant to sanctify the people because God is holy
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:44-45 explains that the dietary laws are part of God's call for His people to be holy as He is holy, indicating a spiritual purpose beyond mere health or culture.

questions.question: What does Leviticus 11:26-27 teach about animals that divide the hoof but do not chew the cud and those that walk on paws?
options: Their carcasses are unclean and cause impurity upon contact
They are considered clean and may be eaten
They symbolize sin and must be sacrificed
They may be eaten if properly washed
questions.correctAnswer: Their carcasses are unclean and cause impurity upon contact
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:26-27 states that animals which divide the hoof but don’t chew the cud, and those walking on paws, are unclean and cause impurity when touched.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 11:46-47 summarize the theological purpose of the entire chapter?
options: To distinguish between clean and unclean creatures, teaching holiness
To provide a zoological classification system
To emphasize the importance of animal sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: To distinguish between clean and unclean creatures, teaching holiness
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:46-47 states the law is to make a difference between clean and unclean animals, underscoring holiness and separation as key theological themes.

questions.question: What synthesis of Leviticus 11:4-6 and Leviticus 11:7 teaches about God's standards for clean animals?
options: Animals must both chew the cud and have divided hooves to be clean
Animals that only chew the cud are clean
Animals with divided hooves are clean regardless of cud chewing
questions.correctAnswer: Animals must both chew the cud and have divided hooves to be clean
questions.explanation: Verses 4-6 describe animals that chew cud but don't divide the hoof as unclean, while verse 7 notes swine divide the hoof but do not chew cud and are unclean, showing both traits are required.

questions.question: According to Leviticus 11:41-42, what is the theological reason for forbidding the consumption of all creeping things that go upon the belly or have many feet?
options: They are abominations and cause defilement
questions.correctAnswer: They are abominations and cause defilement
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:41-42 declares these creeping things as abominations that defile, emphasizing God's command for purity and separation from defilement.

questions.question: How does Leviticus 11:28 and 35 illustrate the consequences of contact with unclean animals in terms of cultic objects and utensils?
options: Objects that contact unclean carcasses become unclean and must be washed or broken
Objects remain clean regardless of contact
Only food utensils are affected, not other objects
The objects must be burned immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Objects that contact unclean carcasses become unclean and must be washed or broken
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11:28 and 35 describe that any vessel or utensil touched by unclean carcasses becomes unclean, requiring washing or destruction to maintain holiness.

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative does Leviticus 11 contribute to, as seen through the theme of distinguishing clean and unclean animals?
options: God’s call for His people to be holy and set apart as a covenant community
The establishment of dietary health codes
The origin of human dietary preferences
questions.correctAnswer: God’s call for His people to be holy and set apart as a covenant community
questions.explanation: Leviticus 11’s distinctions between clean and unclean animals symbolize God’s call for Israel to be holy and separate, a key element in the covenant relationship and redemptive history.
